claims.text: Overall wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu thin coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by its grain-boundary structure and evolution.
Microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu thin coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by its grain-boundary structure and evolution.
Varying annealing temperature and time changes the coating's grain-boundary structure.
The relevant high-temperature sliding regime is above 500 degrees Celsius.
Thermally activated grain-boundary diffusion contributes to the proposed behavior.
Sliding induces grain-boundary migration in the coating.
An optimized grain-boundary structure will improve wear resistance relative to the as-deposited coating.
An optimized grain-boundary structure will reduce microscopic deformation relative to the as-deposited coating.
The as-deposited baseline coating has a random grain-boundary structure.
Failure to find a significant correlation between grain-boundary structure and wear resistance or deformation would falsify the hypothesis.
